title: WedgeBench method transfer through Tabula Rasa v2.10
provenance: Publisher-produced existing records; not independently rerun for publication. No executable distribution or semantic certification.

v2.4.content:
V2.3 REVIEW -> V2.4 REPAIR LEDGER
1. Proposal leakage/history/outside actor: explicit narrow present-action grammar,
proposal frame for every recognized mode, required original-frame coverage.
Evidence: test_revision and development/parser-corpus.json. Unsupported forms
abstain; broad coverage remains an open qualification gate.
2. Eligibility ambiguity: separate envelope, typed schema, contract and evidence
errors; primary_eligible is complete transport + whole-notice schema_valid.
S+A now explicit validation_filter; processable never means semantic acceptance.
Evidence: test_revision eligibility and filter tests; Scoring-Contract.txt.
3. Diagnostics masquerading as abstention: rejection status=null; stable return
keys; indexed anonymous-row audits; separate primary/raw/organizer views.
Evidence: test_boundary, test_grading, serialized full boundary replay.
4. Label/protocol conflict: consolidated protocol; identical label text embedded
in prompt and Annotation-Guide; issuer request vs reported commenter distinction;
acceptable-label set membership, separately assessed scope and issuer.
5. WedgeBench oracle weakness: fixed expectations for field mutations, full-record
boundary controls, parser disposition controls, reproducible hashed receipt.
6. Freshness: exposed cases retired; no new real cases or old confirmation contents
included. Preparation only, no claim of an already completed preregistration.

OPEN BEFORE EXPERIMENT
Independent development qualification (20 positive/20 negative controls and
predeclared coverage/retention gates); stronger conventional baseline adequacy;
exact model/revision and context limits; prospective fresh selection; full source
sufficiency and table exclusion audit; two independent human annotations and
adjudication; operational masking; strict raw transport/duplicate-key collector;
applicable credit verification/cash protection; owner approval for exact release.
No correction here closes these gates or supplies learned-memory evidence.

v2.5.content:
V2.4 REVIEW -> V2.5 REPAIR LEDGER
1. CONFIRMED dropped quotation/condition across paragraphs: context_supported
checks every substantive notice block against a closed grammar. Unknown context
before OR after actions, colon-free qualifications, paraphrased attribution and
intervening prose all cause abstention. Dangling list headers also abstain. All unknown source blocks stay available
in D's abstention evidence. No new claim of general semantic parsing is made.
Evidence: context-corpus.json, test_v25, complete D/G record replay.
Tradeoff: harmless background and undeclared list items also force abstention;
likely material coverage loss, explicitly subject to unchanged qualification.
2. CONFIRMED wrong-notice display: build_views now consumes integrity-checked
prepare_record records. Transport/envelope-invalid responses cannot appear as
ordinary answers. Evidence: full presentation-corpus.json expectations and all-arm
wrong-notice, duplicate/missing/anonymous/unknown-ID tests.
3. CONFIRMED missing diagnostic join: organizer view now preserves transport,
full structural audit, filter audit, eligibility and presentation eligibility.
Top audit=[] cannot hide its cause. Local rejection stays distinct from abstain.
Evidence: tests for local shape, citation/date, transport and top-level failures.
4. Same raw S required: A/G are computed from saved S; view building rejects
modified diagnostics or mismatched S/A/G source text/completion state.
5. Decoding boundary: saved-text decoder rejects duplicate keys and non-JSON
constants and respects incomplete transport. Actual wire collection/attestation
is not implemented and remains an admission gate; no experiment runner exists.
6. Endpoint categories: label_outcome prevents consumers from mistaking a bare
membership Boolean for material-error scoring; scope/evidence remain human work.
7. Blank-line dispute: policy remains blank separators allowed, substantive
non-item resets inheritance. Updated docstring and protocol agree. Prior compact
review lacked the full protocol; its physical-adjacency demand is not adopted as
an automatically established semantic requirement.
8. Unreproduced reviewer claims: slash/colon helper matching and hypothetical
quote-splicing are not reported as proven full-parser failures. No unnecessary
semantic change was made based only on those allegations.

OPEN BEFORE EXPERIMENT
Independent 20-positive/20-negative qualification with unchanged >=80% coverage
and retention/zero-false-commitment gates; baseline adequacy; exact model/context;
prospective fresh selection; source sufficiency; two independent human gold
records; operational masking; live transport attestation/integration; verified
experiment credits/cash protection; owner's exact-version execution approval.
No fixes were tested on real candidate or confirmation contents.

v2.6.content:
V2.5 REVIEW -> V2.6 REPAIRS
1. Practicality: replaced document-wide unknown-prose rejection with explicit
field/section recognition plus retained-context screening. Adjacent headers,
wrapped action text, neutral background/admin fields and exact summary actions
are supported. Whole-document evidence required for structured D/G commitments.
Limit: context screening remains heuristic; implied/novel governing language is
an unresolved risk for independent qualification, not claimed solved semantics.
2. Alias/scope collision: analyze_document is shared by gate and binder; scope
text matching another target alias no longer disables item inheritance. The
reproduced Section 1 / Part 2 case now withdraws only the item, abstaining on
Part 2. This fixes false abstention without making the parent a withdrawn item.
3. Unicode preservation: utf-8-surrogatepass hashes saved text deterministically;
literal and decoded lone surrogates yield explicit transport failures with raw
text retained. No uncaught UnicodeEncodeError and no wire-byte-hash claim.
4. Uniform primary display: S/D schema rejects and A/G null-status rejects are
all answer=null. Internal rejection records and organizer error categories remain
intact. Actual model/filter abstentions remain status=abstain, not no-answer.
5. WedgeBench method: complete-record structured-source oracles plus inherited
boundary/context/presentation replay; new Unicode and uniform-view tests.
No code or fixture was tested on confirmation contents or real evaluation cases.

OPEN GATES
Independent conventional baseline adequacy and source-profile qualification;
unchanged 20-positive/20-negative, >=80% coverage/retention and zero-false-commitment
gates; exact model/context; prospective fresh selection; source sufficiency and
human gold; live transport completion/wire-byte preservation; operational masking;
funding protection and owner approval. G agreement remains non-certifying.

v2.7.content:
V2.6 REVIEW -> V2.7 REPAIR / DESIGN-CHANGE LEDGER
1. Reproduced litigant-demand false commitment: retained as a known lexical
candidate error, not patched with more words. Public compare/G require two
source-bound authenticated independent context attestations. Missing, contradicted
or uncertain support abstains. Candidate diagnostic verdict renamed to
candidate_agreement; actual G uses context_attested, never verified.
2. Summary-only concern: operative_corroboration is required in each review and
must cover a matching non-summary action. Two fixture signatures cannot promote
summary-only text. Partial withdrawal is assessed at exact target scope; no blanket
unresolved rule was introduced.
3. Authentication/independence: HMAC signatures, version/packet/candidate hashes,
trusted registry role/group checks, exactly two reviews; stale/forged/duplicate/
extra/conflicting records withhold. Key authenticity is not semantic truth or
proof of actual human independence. No genuine reviews or keys provisioned.
4. Formal date contract: response-schema.json permits null/string; other JSON
types now schema errors. Non-null strings remain contract errors and raw-S
semantic-scoreable. This is a prospective v2.7 change, not a v2.6 regression claim.
5. Masking: internal views no longer intended for grader delivery. Exact same
answers deduplicated per notice/target, shuffled per grader, arm IDs/counts omitted,
full source retained. Private propagation preserves all original rows/diagnostics.
No-answer semantic grades are null, not errors. Actual masking effectiveness is
unmeasured; access/identity controls remain admission gates.
6. Assistance is explicit: D_R/G now include independent human context work.
This requires Council approval as a changed comparison design. No claim that an
automated stronger contextual baseline has been implemented or qualified.

OPEN GATES
Actual contextual reviewer enrollment/independence, secure key management and
review logging; separate gold and primary graders; operational masked delivery;
independent qualification and automated-baseline adequacy; source sufficiency;
exact model/context; prospective selection; transport collector; verified credits,
cash protection and owner exact-version experiment approval. All remain unmet.

v2.8.content:
v2.8 CHANGES AGAINST THE v2.7 COUNCIL FINDINGS
1. Release binding: context records explicitly include release_sha256; packet digest
also binds exact hashes of implementation and normative procedures. Same-version
byte edits invalidate approvals. A new process and immutable release directory are
required. External pinning of Council-approved release remains an operational gate.
2. Grading propagation: join requires an independently retained digest captured at
trusted construction before dispatch. The whole bundle is bound, including source,
answers, private map, items, reviewer assignments, eligibility and arm identity.
Deletion, duplication, redirection and coordinated edits fail before lock. A digest
from an untrusted caller or newly calculated at join is not an acceptable anchor.
3. Complete grades: substantive statuses require four boolean judgments. Absence
requires label/scope/evidence booleans and issuer N/A. Abstain/no-answer require all
N/A and explanatory notes. Both grader judgments stay separate. False is valid;
blank notes and partial/null substantive judgments cannot lock.
4. Explicit policy: unknown-review entries reject the whole envelope; committed
candidates receive review_envelope_rejected, distinct from context_withheld. This
retains conservative withholding and records the Council's availability concern.
5. Strict metadata: non-JSON and nonfinite context metadata is rejected. v2.7's
alleged universal NaN failure was not reproduced; this is input hardening, not a
claim that that allegation was correct.
6. D_R/G must share identical context records. Duplicate arm kinds and empty arm
sets are rejected. Normative counting uses unique response/target denominators;
overlapping schema/contract diagnostics are not added as independent failures.
7. Architecture unchanged: candidate filter cannot recover missing parser actions;
report anchoring, coverage, missing corroboration and human effort separately.

Evidence: 118 test methods including 14 new v2.8 methods; 38 existing synthetic
controls retain substantive expected outcomes. Fixture authentication metadata is
renewed for the new release only. No genuine human reviews or independent test
set. No real-source selection, confirmation opening or experiment.

v2.9.content:
v2.9 FIX LEDGER — response to v2.8 Council review

1. Approval pin enforcement (all reviewers' shared concern)
release_binding.approved_release requires explicit independently retained pin;
require_approved_release compares exact covered-file fingerprint. Context validation
and grading freeze/validation are protected. Missing, wrong or changed releases
fail. No default local self-approval. Fixtures explicitly simulate approval.
Rechecks detect disk changes instead of caching stale hashes. Immutable deployment
and fresh-process execution remain necessary; file hashes alone cannot prove
executed-code integrity under arbitrary mutation or hostile administration.

2. Durable accepted grades (Claude/Gemini condition; OpenAI scope distinction)
Pure helper renamed validate_primary_grades; it returns validation_complete=True,
primary_locked=False. Public join now requires organizer ledger and registered
batch ID. SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE plus unique acceptance key persists one result;
receipt binds release, manifest, exact submitted grades and validated output.
Copied bundles, fresh processes and concurrent calls cannot replace acceptance in
the same store. Repeated requests fail; read-only receipt recovery is explicit.
No in-memory Boolean is relied on. Distinct outputs were already distinguishable;
this repair adds durable authority for which one was accepted, not a false claim
that all prior outputs looked identical. No silent amendment API.

3. Upstream invariant validation (Gemini and Claude conditions)
Before freeze, validate_grading_bundle checks the two reviewer batches, exact
original arm/notice/target coverage, unique item/map correspondence, source/target
provenance, deduplication, closed status values and diagnostic coverage. Post-freeze
hash comparison still binds eligibility and all original data. Structurally valid
fabricated inputs remain a trusted-construction/actor issue, not solved by hashing.

4. Tests and evidence
15 new controls alongside 118 inherited methods; 38 inherited replay cases retain
substantive expected outcomes, with renewed public fixture release bindings only.
Legacy join tests now target pure validate_primary_grades and expect no lock.
New end-to-end store tests cover actual locking, replay across process restart,
concurrency, rollback, SQL update/delete refusal and accepted-receipt integrity.
No production approval, enrolled reviewers or independent qualification claimed.

NOT PERFORMED
No Council submission, experimental generation, source selection, confirmation
access, production store deployment, live review key issuance or GitHub publication.

v2.10.content:
v2.10 FIX LEDGER — SQL replacement finding from the v2.9 Council review

Confirmed prior behavior: INSERT OR REPLACE could overwrite existing batches and
accepted records when recursive_triggers=0, bypassing delete-trigger protections.
The protected Python API itself rejected repeat acceptance; the defect was the
broader ordinary-SQL guarantee. External retained receipt hashes exposed changes.

Repair
- BEFORE INSERT guards reject existing authority identity, batch ID or manifest,
  and accepted-grade batch ID, before SQLite resolves the conflict by replacement.
- Manifest conflicts are protected even under a different batch ID, including a
  collision with two different existing records.
- WITHOUT ROWID tables remove the implicit rowid/_rowid_/oid conflict path. Batch
  and acceptance keys are explicitly NOT NULL; authority identity remains 1.
- Update/delete triggers remain. Conflict rejection applies even to OR IGNORE and
  UPSERT; recovery uses read_acceptance, not an attempted duplicate insert.
- Store format 210 is enforced on open and protected operations. No silent migration
  of v2.9 stores. The format marker is compatibility checking, not proof against
  privileged schema manipulation.

Evidence
Eight new test methods (141 total) test separate writer connections with recursive
triggers OFF/ON and foreign keys OFF, normal REPLACE and INSERT OR REPLACE, primary
and unique-manifest conflicts, UPSERT, hidden row IDs/null keys, multirow rollback,
fresh-process rejection and receipt preservation, fresh legitimate acceptance and
unsupported-format refusal. The original 133 tests still pass, including acceptance
races, restart replay, failed-grade rollback and approval-gate checks.
38 inherited replay controls preserve their substantive expected outcomes. Only
public fixture authentication bindings are renewed for this exact release.

Boundary
New nonconflicting direct SQL inserts do not become genuine registrations or grades.
Organizer authentication, protected store access, immutable deployment and external
receipt copies remain necessary. No claim against trigger/schema removal, disabled
enforcement, writable_schema, file replacement/rollback or privileged attackers.
No parser redesign, experiment, independent qualification or production deployment.

replay_selection_policy: All 38 recorded synthetic development replay observations; not a runnable distribution.

content.reviewer_exposure: Contract and public interfaces only; no implementation, author tests, execution results or prior Council code assessments.
content.scope: Mechanical SQL/approval/acceptance qualification using fresh synthetic stores; not human semantic qualification.
content.execution_operator: Original implementation assistant; independently designed tests, not independent human execution.

cases: A: Seed authority, B1/M1, B2/M2, accepted B1/R1. Separate connections/processes, recursive_triggers OFF/ON: REPLACE, INSERT OR REPLACE/IGNORE and UPSERT against each identity; B3/M1 and B1/M2 collisions; UPDATE/DELETE; NULL keys; hidden-rowid insertion. Expect rejection and unchanged originals/R1. Valid-first/conflicting-second multirow insert leaves no new row.

B: Register B normally. Barrier two processes accepting distinct valid grades; expect one committed acceptance. Retain winning receipt privately, suppress delivery, terminate/restart. Same-pin read returns exactly that receipt/payload/hashes; retry cannot overwrite.

C: Missing/wrong approval pins and wrong-pin opening refuse; existing-path creation refuses. Registered B: independently specified invalid grades fail without consumption; valid copied-bundle submission succeeds; changed-grade retry fails, preserving original grades/receipt.
cases.boundary: Older/unknown formats refuse opening/protected operations without mutation.

cases: A: fresh store pin P; register('b1',X)->M1; accept('b1',X,G)->R1. Separate raw connection, recursive_triggers OFF then ON: INSERT OR REPLACE batches('b1',M2) and ('b2',M1); REPLACE accepted('b1'); UPSERT accepted('b1') DO UPDATE; INSERT OR IGNORE authority(1); multirow INSERT batches('b9',M9),('b1',M1x); UPDATE batches WHERE 'b1'; DELETE accepted 'b1'; NULL-key insert; rowid insert. Expect: every statement raises; counts unchanged; 'b9' absent; read_acceptance('b1').receipt_sha256==R1; authority row byte-identical.

B: two fresh processes open with P, barrier, both accept('b2',X2,G) with distinct grade sets. Expect exactly one receipt, other raises conflict; read_acceptance('b2')==winner after restart. Lost response: SIGKILL after commit before return -> read_acceptance('b3') returns receipt whose hashes recompute from bundle, retry raises conflict. Kill before commit -> not-found, registration present, retry succeeds exactly once. Copied bundle preserves recovery.

C: approved_release(None)/wrong sha raise; create() on existing path raises; wrong pin refuses open. register('b4',X4); malformed grades (missing key, wrong type, unknown item) raise; 'b4' registration present, read_acceptance not-found; valid accept succeeds once; accept('b4',Y≠X4) refused; later accept('b4',X4,G2) and raw UPDATE/DELETE on accepted('b4') refused; read_acceptance returns original grade-set hash and receipt_sha256.
cases.boundary: Boundary/control: open synthetic format-209/unrecognized store -> refused, file bytes unchanged (from A/C); raw INSERT fabricated nonconflicting accepted('b_fake') -> SQLite accepts, recorded as documented out-of-guarantee limit, not pass; then DROP TRIGGER and rerun A to prove the harness can fail.

cases: Case A (SQL/Rollback): Setup format-210 store; register B1(M1), B2(M2); accept B1->R1. Ops: On separate SQL connections with recursive_triggers OFF/ON, attempt REPLACE/UPSERT/INSERT OR IGNORE on authority(1), batches(B1,M3), batches(B3,M1), dual-row collision batches(B1,M2), accepted(B1), NULL keys, rowid references, UPDATE/DELETE, and multirow insert [valid B4, conflicting B1]. Expect: All raise errors; B4 rolls back; B1/B2/R1/authority unchanged.

Case B (Concurrency/Recovery): Setup store with pin P; register B1(M1), B2(M2). Ops: Barrier two fresh processes racing accept(B1,M1,G1) vs accept(B1,M1,G2); simulate lost response by killing winner after commit before return, restart with P, call read_acceptance(B1) using copied bundle, retry accept(B1); kill B2 before commit, restart, verify registration survives, retry accept(B2). Expect: One B1 winner (R1), loser/retry raise conflict; read_acceptance(B1)==R1; B2 retry succeeds once.

Case C (Pins/Grades): Setup store with pin P; register B1(M1). Ops: Call approved_release/open with missing/wrong pin; create() on existing path; accept(B1,M1,invalid_grades); accept(B1,M_wrong,valid_G1); accept(B1,copied_M1,valid_G1)->R1; retry accept(B1,M1,valid_G2). Expect: Bad pins, existing path, wrong manifest, and invalid grades rejected without consuming B1; valid_G1 succeeds once; retry rejected; read_acceptance(B1) preserves exact R1 and grade-set hash.
cases.boundary: Format/Control Boundary: Refuse older/unknown format (e.g., 209) at open and protected ops without mutation; verify raw nonconflicting SQL insert succeeds (documenting out-of-scope boundary) and dropping triggers causes Case A to fail (negative harness control).

interpretations: Use final revised plans. The initial suggestion that a copied registered bundle can be registered under a new ID in the same store is not adopted: the contract explicitly prohibits repeated manifests.
Crash injection will occur at sqlite connection exit before commit or after successful commit and before public accept returns; only child processes holding temporary stores will be killed.
Trigger removal negative control and fabricated nonconflicting inserts are intentionally out-of-scope controls, never production mutations.
No outcomes observed before this plan lock. Harness coding and execution follow the lock.
